Print and Tidy Resampling Results

Source: R/methods-inference.R
lsa-inference-methods.Rd

Methods for the results of bootstrap_lsa(), permute_lsa() and stability_lsa(). print() shows a header summary: the engine, the number of replicates, the resampling settings, and how many edges are stable or significant. as.data.frame() returns the per-edge table described under Value of the constructor; transitions() returns the same table and adds significant = and sort = arguments.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'lsa_bootstrap'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'lsa_permutation'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'lsa_stability'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'lsa_bootstrap'
as.data.frame(x, row.names = NULL, optional = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'lsa_permutation'
as.data.frame(x, row.names = NULL, optional = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'lsa_stability'
as.data.frame(x, row.names = NULL, optional = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

x

An lsa_bootstrap, lsa_permutation or lsa_stability object.

row.names, optional, ...

Ignored; present for consistency with the generics.

Value

print() returns x invisibly. as.data.frame() returns a data.frame with one row per from -> to cell: the bootstrap, permutation or stability columns listed in bootstrap_lsa(), permute_lsa() and stability_lsa().

See also

transitions()

Examples

fit <- lsa(engagement)
st <- stability_lsa(fit, R = 20)
st
#> <lsa_stability>
#>   engine:        classical
#>   replicates:    20
#>   proportion:    80%
#>   min stable:    95%
#>   stable edges:  7 of 9 (>= 95% across replicates)
head(as.data.frame(st))
#>         from      to observed_sig stability stable
#> 1     Active  Active         TRUE      1.00   TRUE
#> 2    Average  Active         TRUE      1.00   TRUE
#> 3 Disengaged  Active         TRUE      1.00   TRUE
#> 4     Active Average         TRUE      1.00   TRUE
#> 5    Average Average         TRUE      1.00   TRUE
#> 6 Disengaged Average        FALSE      0.15  FALSE
